Definition: from the alternate of G2192; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition:--fashion.
BiblicalUsage: Schema is fashion, the outward shape of things, and Paul uses it twice to opposite ends: the fashion of this world passeth away, so use the world as not abusing it; and Christ made Himself of no reputation and was made in the likeness of men, taking the fashion of a servant.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the world's fashion passes, but the Servant's fashion stays — Christ took our shape to save us, and we are not to cling to a shape that is passing away.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
